scope: PR #272 (#270) only: src/lib/LibRainDeployClone.sol (A), the checkZoltuFactory / checkDeclaredDependencies / zoltuDeployStep / deployStepToNetworks / rememberDeployer surface of src/lib/LibRainDeploy.sol (B), src/abstract/RainDeployCloneSuitesBase.sol (C), src/abstract/RainDeployCloneBroadcast.sol (D)
notes: 58 mutants over four units, 57 KILLED and 1 equivalent, baseline green at 695 before this run's tests and 698 after. Every verdict in this entry was read back from a per-run log retained under .mutation-test/runs/ with its exit status in a trailer; no verdict here rests on a tally alone.

The harness was minting FALSE KILLS, and that is the main finding of this run. .env holds public endpoints and says so in its own header: 'These are public endpoints and they rate-limit. CI holds its own.' When one answers HTTP 429 a forge fork test fails at gas 0 having executed nothing, the tally goes red, and mutation-probe scores any red tally as KILLED. So a rate-limited run mints a kill for a mutation nothing caught, and a false kill cannot be told apart from coverage the suite does not have.

check.sh now classifies a red tally before reporting it. A failure carrying a transport signature (an HTTP status, an exhausted retry budget, a fork that could not be instantiated, an account that could not be read) is a failed READ, not a failed assertion. Any genuine failure present is reported immediately and never retried, so the guard cannot hide a mutant the suite really caught; a tally that is ALL transport is retried after the 60s rate-limit window; and if it is still all-transport after three attempts the proof tally is deliberately WITHHELD so the probe records NO-RUN, which is unscorable and honest, rather than a false KILLED.

The guard earned itself twice in this run. The 50-mutant pass's own BASELINE went red on transport errors on its first two attempts and came back green at 698 on the third; under the previous harness the probe would have aborted on a red baseline and the whole pass would have been lost. It also rescued C07, whose first attempt was red from flake alone and whose retry was cleanly green, so it scored SURVIVED instead of a false KILLED.

The predecessor pass's D01 SURVIVED / D02 KILLED contradiction is resolved, and the resolution inverts it: D02 was never killed. Its run went red on exactly one failure, LibRainDeployTest::testDeployToNetworksAbsentDependencyDeclaringNoCodeIsStillMissing(), a 429 at gas 0 in a Zoltu-path fork test that never touches the clone broadcast. The same reading disposes of the other two kills in that pass: A27's run was 21 failures all 429 at gas 0, and B09's single failure was LibHyperCoreTest::testCreditOnAHyperEvmFork() with an HTTP 400 'Unknown block'. Across all nine logs of that pass the count of failures that were NOT transport errors was ZERO, so the pass contained no genuine kills at all and all eight of its mutants had in fact survived. Nothing about D01's mutation was malformed, and there was no contradiction to explain once the kills were seen for what they were.

Two earlier explanations were tested and refuted rather than carried forward. A 403 in a run log is not disqualifying on its own: logs with 403s still report a full green tally. And 'the tally went red' is not the signal either, which is what mistook flake for coverage. The signal is whether a failure is an assertion or a failed read. A structural explanation was also refuted directly: no test in the suite reads RainDeployCloneBroadcast.sol's AST or ABI — the four structure tests target CreditHyperCore, BuildScript and AddressRegistryGet, and the only reference to that file anywhere in test/ is ExampleCloneDeploy's import of it.

All 50 mutants from batches A, B and C were re-probed under the fixed harness, because their original verdicts predate log retention and so name no killer that can be read back, and because the harness that produced them has since been shown to mint false kills — a verdict with no log behind it cannot be distinguished from one of those in either direction. The re-probe was warranted: C07, which batch C had recorded as KILLED with no killer at all, SURVIVED. Batch A had also used a non-greedy fail-pattern that stops at the first ']' inside a FAIL line, and batches B and C captured only test-prefixed names, which silently drops a setUp() failure; both are corrected.

C07 ('cloneDeployByName reads the clone list past its empty guard', replacing checkedCloneDeploys() with cloneDeploys()) is an EQUIVALENT mutant, not a coverage gap, and is recorded as such rather than closed with a test that could not discriminate. testNoCloneDeploysReverts already drives that reader on an empty declaration and expects NoCloneDeploys. Under the mutation the empty list is no longer refused at the top, so control reaches 'revert UnknownDeploymentSuite(requested, suiteNames())' — but suiteNames() calls allSuites(), which calls checkedCandidateSuites(), which calls candidateSuites(), which calls checkedCloneDeploys(). The revert's own argument re-enters the guard and raises NoCloneDeploys first, so the observable error is identical and no external test can tell the two apart. Worth knowing that the invariant is enforced on that path by the revert argument rather than by the direct call, which is a fragile equivalence: it would become observable if suiteNames() ever stopped routing through checkedCloneDeploys(). The code as written calls checkedCloneDeploys() directly, which is correct and is what its NatSpec states, so this is a note and not a defect.

Pre-existing regression worth fixing at the source: the 2026-10-06 entry in this file records repointing .env to tenderly and drpc 'after which the baseline was stable at 668 and every mutant scored'. .env is generated from script/Build.sol's public defaults between its markers, so regenerating it silently reverted that repointing — ARBITRUM_RPC_URL is back on arb1.arbitrum.io and ETHEREUM_RPC_URL on eth-pokt.nodies.app, the exact endpoint that entry names as flaky. The harness guard above makes the probe trustworthy on public endpoints but does not make them reliable; a durable fix is a non-public endpoint for local fork runs, which this run had no credentials for.

Eight gaps were closed by three new tests and three strengthened in place. testCloneDeployStepRefusesThePredictionBeforeBroadcasting (A21) pins the ORDER of the prediction guard, which the existing mismatch test structurally cannot: its refusal reverts the whole external call, so a clone already broadcast is rolled back with it and code.length == 0 afterwards is true whether the guard ran first or last. The new MockUncloneableMispredictingCloneFactory mispredicts AND cannot clone, so reaching the broadcast window answers CloneWasReached and CloneFactoryPredictionMismatch coming back instead is proof nothing was broadcast. testDeployStepToNetworksNoNetworksReverts (B09) asks the shared loop directly, which nothing above it can do on its behalf since deployToNetworks, deployAndBroadcast, cloneToNetworks and cloneAndBroadcast all carry the same guard. testBroadcastSuiteHandsOverTheSelectedCloneAndTheRecordedAddress (D01, D02, D03) stales the recorded address so one error names both the address handed over and the address the selected clone derives. The three strengthened in place: cloneToNetworks' empty-list test now stales the declared address (with an agreeing one, NoNetworks still comes back from the shared loop's guard), cloneAndBroadcast's now passes a zero key so 'refused before the key is remembered' is observable, and testCloneAndBroadcastReachesEveryNetwork now asserts the forge wallet holds the deploy key, which is the only way to see a deployer derived without being remembered.

Attribution: every behaviour in scope is new on this branch, so there is no older suite to credit and no pre-existing-suite pass was possible. killedByExistingTests counts the 49 mutants whose killer list names at least one test already committed on this branch before this run; none of the 49 was killed only by a test this run added or strengthened, so each would have been killed at the scanned commit too. gapsFilled counts the 8 that survived at the scanned commit and are killed at testsAfterCommit. The matrix establishes that this PR's tests discriminate, not which older test covered what.
No adversarial findings were filed. The adversarial pass's one candidate was C07's fragile equivalence, which is a note above rather than an issue because the current behaviour is correct.
